evidence: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy showed that the films grown at lower temperatures have a smaller bandgap energy. The impurity content in the films was investigated by Auger electron spectroscopy (AES) and XPS. Impurities, such as residual H, OH, and C, were investigated by time of flight secondary-ion mass spectroscopy (ToF-SIMS) using Cs+ sputtering. The film thickness and refractive index (n) were measured by spectroscopic ellipsometry. The dielectric constant was estimated from the accumulation capacitance of the C-V curves. The C-V curves show well-defined accumulation and depletion regions, suggesting reasonably good interface properties. The J-E curves of Al2O3 films grown at various Tg with O3 and H2O as reactant, respectively, were analyzed. The O 1s core-level spectra of the Al2O3 films were analyzed using XPS.
